context:
Goal: the feedback log catches real repeats without false alarms.
Problem (rule): the repeat judge is a ruled guard (your ruling 2026-11-01 17:57 CST), and 8 of 8 marks today were false; only you can change a ruled guard.
Based on (measured): 8 marks, 0 true, in the retrospective session, 11:53-12:58 CST; one Stop gave 3 new items the same candidate, and it matched the session's own follow-up items to its own earlier block on the same thread.
Based on (ruling): your 12:59 CST question "also you've said this a bunch -- is something wrong herE?".
Departs from: main blocks the Stop on every mark — a mark that points at the item's own home or at the session's own block on the same thread is skipped, and other marks print one line without blocking.
Meanwhile: the retrospective keeps dropping false marks.

options.how: Skip own-thread and own-home matches; other marks print one line and do not block.
options.label: Skip own matches; marks stop blocking (Recommended)
options.lose: A real repeat shows as a note a session could skip.

options.gain: True repeats still force a merge.
options.how: Add the two skips; marks still block the Stop.
options.label: Keep blocking, add the two skips
options.lose: Other false marks still cost turns.

reply: You answered in chat at 13:03 CST (relayed by the retrospective): "yes on the fix !". The check that flags a repeated owner remark skips a match on the item's own home or the same message, gives each item its own matches, prints one line, and never blocks. It still matches by meaning. Home: the decision on the owner feedback inbox (its Repeats part), rewritten in place; roadmap step repeat-judge-never-blocks.
short: Stop the repeat judge's false alarms how?
title: The repeat judge marked 8 items today and none were repeats. Should its marks stop blocking?
why: Each false mark blocks a Stop and costs a turn.
